title: James K. Workman et al. (Session of Peace Presbyterian Church) v. Eastern Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint against Eastern Carolina Presbytery. The judgment did not expressly rescind the Presbytery’s resolution or order further proceedings.
first_summary: The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind a resolution calling total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly sustained the complaint because the resolution went beyond Scripture and, in practice, bound church members’ consciences contrary to the Westminster Confession. The commission nevertheless approved efforts to resist intemperance and encouraged guidance consistent with the Eighth General Assembly.
summary: The Session challenged Eastern Carolina Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its resolution calling voluntary total abstinence from alcohol the proper Christian lifestyle. The General Assembly unanimously sustained the complaint, adopting the commission’s conclusion that the resolution in practice bound consciences and exceeded Scripture’s requirements contrary to the Westminster Confession. The judgment did not expressly rescind the resolution, and it distinguished improper conscience-binding from permissible teaching and counseling against alcohol abuse and intemperance.

sources.supports: General Assembly adoption, undisputed facts, issue, explanatory opinion, unanimous judgment, and qualification concerning intemperance.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The caption identifies the parties; the commission’s report was approved as the General Assembly’s action and judgment (printed pp. 109–110, lines 31–41).
evidence_notes.dispute: The complaint challenged Presbytery’s refusal to rescind its total-abstinence resolution as exceeding Scripture and binding conscience (printed pp. 57, 110, lines 13–23, 59–67).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The commission found that members would feel bound by the resolution and unanimously sustained the complaint (printed pp. 110–111, lines 69–81).
evidence_notes.qualifications: The commission applauded moral guidance, urged reliance on the Eighth Assembly’s approach, and affirmed vigorous resistance to intemperance; no express rescission order appears (printed p. 111, lines 75–91).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: The opinion endorsed the Eighth General Assembly’s guidance; its relevant conclusion—that denominational total abstinence exceeded Scripture and contravened WCF 20.2—is reproduced in the facts (printed p. 110, lines 53–55, 69–73).

source_limits: The supplied record reproduces the relevant earlier Assembly conclusion but not its complete underlying minutes. It provides no express remedial order beyond sustaining the complaint.

score_reasons.concrete_dispute: Identifies the refusal to rescind the total-abstinence resolution.
score_reasons.decision: States the unanimous sustaining of the complaint without inventing rescission or remand.
score_reasons.decisive_reason: Explains that the resolution practically bound conscience beyond Scripture and the Confession.
score_reasons.distinctive_value: Preserves the distinction between binding conscience and counseling against abuse or intemperance.
score_reasons.fidelity: Separates the adopted judgment, its reasoning, and its nonoperative commendation.
score_reasons.economy: Retains only facts necessary to understand the issue, result, reason, and limitation.

verification_notes: Rechecked the Assembly’s adoption at lines 33–35, the conscience-binding rationale at lines 69–73, and the operative judgment at lines 75–81. The final summary clarifies that sustaining the complaint did not expressly rescind the resolution and adds the adopted distinction permitting teaching against abuse and intemperance.
